China's Central Bank to Investigate Solana's Advertising Campaign in Shanghai's Lujiazui District An official from the People's Bank of China (PBOC) said authorities recently discovered that Solana had placed advertisements in Shanghai's Lujiazui financial district through domestic entities, using brand promotion to market cryptocurrencies. The PBOC, together with local financial regulators, police, and market supervision authorities, has halted the planned Solana Accelerate China 2026 events in Shanghai and other cities and will investigate the entities and individuals involved. The official stated that Solana's promotional activities violated the notice issued by eight Chinese authorities in February 2026 on preventing and addressing risks related to cryptocurrencies. The PBOC will continue targeting domestic cryptocurrency trading businesses and China-based affiliates of overseas cryptocurrency issuance and trading platforms. — link

WuBlockchain Weekly: Democrats Win Congress, Binance Details $6.34B Hack, Vitalik Warns of Crypto Security Risks Democrats won both chambers of Congress as crypto markets plunged. Binance detailed its $6.34B hack involving fake job interviews and compromised AI tools. Vitalik urged the industry to prioritize survival. Hong Kong passed new crypto tax reporting rules, Circle reported $865M in quarterly revenue, and Tether disclosed holdings of 150,000 BTC. ICE's Hyperliquid initiative remains subject to regulatory approval. For the full weekly roundup, subscribe to our Substack: — link

Former FBI Agent Admits Stealing $2.47M in Crypto Linked to 35 Investigations, Faces Up to 20 Years in Prison Former FBI agent Patrick Steven Yaroch pleaded guilty to wire fraud and money laundering after stealing approximately $2.47 million in cryptocurrency through about 100 unauthorized transfers involving 35 FBI investigations, according to the U.S. Department of Justice. Some funds belonged to at least 10 financial crime victims. Yaroch used stolen funds to repay personal debts and consulted ChatGPT about relocating to Europe, including plans to buy a vineyard in Portugal. Sentencing is scheduled for March 4, 2027, with a maximum penalty of 20 years in prison. — link

US October Nonfarm Payrolls Rise by 165K, Beating 65K Forecast U.S. nonfarm payrolls rose by 165,000 in October, beating expectations of 65,000, according to the Bureau of Labor Statistics. September's figure was revised up from 29,000 to 60,000. The unemployment rate fell to 4.1%, below the 4.2% forecast and previous reading. Average hourly earnings increased 0.4% month-over-month and 3.1% year-over-year, both above expectations of 0.3% and 2.9%, respectively. — link
